fields.features_heading: A Quote Request That Arrives Ready to Price
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the form, the price tiers behind it, and the routing that puts termite and business jobs in front of a person.
fields.feature_1:
Questions that start with the pest

Customers pick the pest first, then say where in the building they saw it and upload a photo if they have one. Picking termites swaps the price for an inspection booking.
fields.feature_2:
A price drawn from square footage

Set a first-visit price for each square footage tier you quote. A homeowner sees the price for their tier on screen before submitting, so the phone call opens on a number.
fields.feature_3:
Photos of the pest or the damage

An optional upload takes a picture of droppings, mud tubes, or a wasp nest. The technician opens the request and sees the photo beside the address before driving out.
fields.feature_4:
Commercial jobs reach a person

Choose Business as the property type and the form shows no price. Instead it emails the request to the person who writes commercial contracts, who quotes for that building.
fields.feature_5:
Reminders on quotes nobody answered

Pick how many days a quote can sit unanswered. Past that point the customer gets one email reminder, and the owner gets a short list of every quote that was nudged that day.
fields.feature_6:
Requests in a database you own

Every request lands as a row in a database you own, with the pest, the address, and the price shown. On paid plans, export the full code to your own GitHub repository.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Pest Control Quote Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to build a pest control quote form that prices home jobs on screen and routes the rest to a person.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Write down every pest you treat
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Decide which answers hide the price
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down every pest your technicians treat, from ants and roaches to rodents and wasps. Each one becomes a choice in the pest question. Add an Other choice too, and send those requests to a person instead of a price.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Pick the square footage breaks you already quote on the phone, such as every 1,000 square feet, and give each one a first-visit price. Round breaks let a homeowner find their tier without measuring again.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Choose the answers that need a visit before a number. Termites can open a list of inspection times. A business property can go by email to whoever writes your commercial contracts.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Put the photo upload right after the question about where the pest was seen. Leave it optional, because a customer who never saw the pest still needs to send the request.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the price tiers and the routing rules into one prompt. Emergent builds the form, the database behind it, and the email alerts. Change a question or a price later by asking in plain English.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Match the reminder window to how fast your crew can fit in a new job, such as 5 days. Send one reminder, not a series. Ask for the day's reminded quotes to reach the owner in one email.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Submit a home under your first break, then a termite job with a photo. Check the price on the first and the inspection times on the second. Finish with a business address and confirm the email reached the commercial manager.

faq_plan.q: What is a pest control quote form?
faq_plan.a: A pest control quote form is a web form where a homeowner or a business describes a pest problem and asks what treatment will cost. It collects the property type, its size, the pest, and where it showed up. The answers either price the job on screen or tell the office exactly what to quote.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a pest control quote form?
faq_plan.a: Set your prices first: what a first visit costs at each home size, and the pests you only quote after an inspection. Then describe the questions, the prices, and who gets each kind of request to Emergent's AI form builder. It builds the form and the database behind it, and you can change any price later by asking.

faq_plan.q: Which pests should a pest control quote form price without an inspection?
faq_plan.a: Price online the pests whose treatment scales with the size of the home, such as ants or roaches. Hold the price for jobs where hidden damage sets the work, such as termites or animals in an attic, and offer an inspection time instead. Write that split down before you build, since the form follows it exactly.

faq_plan.q: How do I set prices by home size on a pest control quote form?
faq_plan.a: Give each square footage tier its own first-visit price and let the form match the customer's answer to a tier. Ask for square footage as a number, never a size word like small or large, so the match is exact. A cleaning quote form prices homes from bedrooms and bathrooms instead; pick whichever measure your crew already quotes from.

faq_plan.q: Can customers upload photos on a pest control quote form?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Add an optional upload to the form, and the photo arrives with the request. A clear shot of droppings or a nest helps the technician pack the right treatment. With Emergent, each photo is saved with its request in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How should a pest control quote form handle termite jobs?
faq_plan.a: Swap the price for a booking: the customer picks an inspection time instead of seeing a number. Add two questions only termite requests see, asking whether the home was treated before and roughly when. The inspector then arrives knowing whether this is a first treatment or a follow-up.

faq_plan.q: Can one pest control quote form handle homes and businesses?
faq_plan.a: Yes, with a property type question at the top that sends each answer down its own path. Homes get a tier price, while business requests skip the price and go to the person who quotes commercial accounts. Soil treatment for a builder before a slab is poured fits better on a construction quote form, which collects measurements and site photos.

faq_plan.q: Who should get the request when a pest control quote form is submitted?
faq_plan.a: Send priced home requests to whoever books the schedule, and business requests to your commercial manager. Name a backup for each route for the days that person is out. The app sends each route its own email or Slack alert the moment the request is saved.

faq_plan.q: What should a pest control quote form ask the customer?
faq_plan.a: Ask only what changes the price or the route: name, email, address, property type, square footage, the pest, where it was seen, and an optional photo. Questions about gate codes or pets in the yard can wait for the booking. Forms built with Emergent have no response caps.

faq_plan.q: How do I follow up on quotes sent from a pest control quote form?
faq_plan.a: Send one email reminder after a set number of days, with the original price and a link back to the quote, then call. For a commercial account that wants written terms, follow up with a proposal form that sets out the scope and the visit schedule instead of a second reminder.
